fatal_errors: The proposed fine, equiaxed, dynamically recrystallized microstructure contradicts the observed as-cast, solidification-segregated W-Ta-rich dendritic and Zr-Ti-rich interdendritic two-BCC-phase structure.
Repeated arc melting is incorrectly treated as a demonstrated dynamic-recrystallization and grain-refinement intervention.
The proposed 1000–1800 °C testing range lies entirely outside the reported room-temperature-to-500 °C mechanical measurements.
The baseline is reconstructed incorrectly: the actual comparator was commercially sourced, powder-sintered coarse-grained tungsten, not tungsten subjected to the same arc-melting routine.
The experiment changes composition and microstructure simultaneously, so it cannot isolate grain refinement as the cause of improved plasticity or toughness.
No prior evidence is cited, and the claimed governing mechanism was not measured or supported by the reported characterization.
explanation: The response aligns only at the broad level of comparing WTaTiVZr with tungsten and predicting improved plastic strain and toughness. It misses the central observed structural mediator and proposed chemistry-based mechanisms: multicomponent solid-solution strengthening and lattice distortion from W/Ta, combined with damage-tolerance contributions associated with Ti/V/Zr in a segregated two-BCC dendritic microstructure. Its fine-grain/dynamic-recrystallization account is inconsistent with the as-cast material. Conditions, baseline processing, and tests are also substantially incorrect. Although the suggested EBSD/TEM and mechanical measurements could test a grain-refinement hypothesis, comparing different compositions does not distinguish refinement effects from chemistry, phase constitution, or segregation. A discriminating design would vary microstructure within WTaTiVZr while holding composition fixed, then compare matched microstructural states and retain the actual RT–500 °C and room-temperature toughness regime.
